title: FIND and SEARCH: case-sensitive or not

docs.syntax: =FIND(needle,text) matches case; =SEARCH(needle,text) ignores it; both answer a position
docs.explain: FIND and SEARCH do the same job and disagree about only one thing: capital letters. That difference is the whole reason both exist, and it decides which one you write. When the text is a code, case is part of the meaning, so a hyphen has to be found as a hyphen and a lower-case letter as a lower-case letter. FIND does that, and it fails loudly when the character it was sent to look for is not there. When the text is a label somebody typed, case is noise, so SEARCH is the right tool. It finds north, North and NORTH wherever they sit in the cell. Both functions answer with a position number counted from the left, not with the text they found, which is what makes them useful inside MID. This lesson pins the difference down with one screen each, so the learner types the same shape twice and only the function name changes.

errors.text: The text being searched for does not occur in the cell.
The function name is misspelled, so the sheet has nothing to call.

docs.atWork: Locating a separator or a word inside a code or a label before slicing it.
docs.outcome: Choose FIND for a case-sensitive position and SEARCH when the case should not matter.
docs.teaches: FIND reporting a case-sensitive position and SEARCH ignoring case
docs.dataset: Hyphenated codes and typed labels holding lower-case letters

screens.prompt: In B2, report the position of the hyphen in the code in A2.

hints.syntax: =FIND("-",A2): the character to look for first, then the text.
hints.func-find: Codes are case-sensitive text, so the position comes from FIND.
hints.value: A, N, then the hyphen: it sits in third place.
hints.error: A character the cell does not hold is a #VALUE! error.

reject.why: SEARCH would answer three too, but this screen is about the case-sensitive function
the length of the code is not the position of the hyphen
the hyphen is in third place, not second
searching from the fourth character misses the hyphen
there is no underscore in the code
the code is typed in rather than read from A2
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In B2, report the position of the first N in the label in A2 whatever its case.

hints.syntax: =SEARCH("N",A2): the character, then the text, with case ignored.
hints.func-search: The label is typed text, so the position comes from SEARCH.
hints.value: b, a, n: the first N is in third place.
hints.error: A letter the label does not hold is a #VALUE! error.

reject.why: FIND is case-sensitive, so it never finds a capital N in this label
the length of the label is not a position
the first A sits in second place
searching from the fourth character finds the second N
the formula reads the third label rather than A2
searching from the fourth character finds the second N
the label is typed in rather than read from A2
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

seo.title: FIND and SEARCH in Excel: case or no case
seo.description: FIND matches capital letters exactly and SEARCH ignores them. Both answer a position counted from the left, which is what makes them useful inside MID.
